regions.name: Malapert Massif
regions.nasaListing: Artemis III candidate region in NASA's Aug 2022 list and its refined list of nine (Oct 28, 2024)

observationPoint.selectionRule: Observation point = of candidate points on a 2 km grid within 15 km of the gazetteer centre, the one where the Sun's centre is above the LOLA terrain horizon for the largest fraction of 2027 (hourly).

horizon.method: Maximum terrain elevation angle along great-circle rays (80 m–150 km), observer 2 m above surface, spherical Moon R=1737.4 km; DEM samples beyond the 80°S product edge ignored.

regional.note: 12×12 block-mean of LDEM_80S_80M; cells outside the 80°S product set to −20 km

notes: Reference feature Mons Malapert: IAU-approved 2024, 67 km across, centred 85.98°S 1.67°W.

regions.name: Nobile Rim 1
regions.nasaListing: Artemis III candidate region in NASA's Aug 2022 list and its refined list of nine (Oct 28, 2024)

observationPoint.selectionRule: NASA has not published coordinates distinguishing 'Rim 1' from 'Rim 2'. Observation point = of 72 rim-crest points (highest point between 0.8 and 1.2 crater radii along radial profiles every 5°), the one with the largest fraction of 2027 hours with the Sun's centre above the LOLA terrain horizon. It is a representative rim location, not necessarily inside the Rim 1 region.

regions.name: Peak near Cabeus B
regions.nasaListing: Artemis III candidate region in NASA's refined list of nine (Oct 28, 2024)

observationPoint.selectionRule: NASA has not published the location of the peak. Observation point = the highest LOLA elevation (3×3-smoothed) between 0.6 and 1.6 crater radii of the Cabeus B centre, i.e. the most prominent peak adjoining the crater. Provisional reference: it may not coincide with the NASA region.

horizon.method: Maximum terrain elevation angle along great-circle rays (80 m–150 km), observer 2 m above surface, spherical Moon R=1737.4 km; DEM samples beyond the 80°S product edge ignored.

regional.note: 12×12 block-mean of LDEM_80S_80M; cells outside the 80°S product set to −20 km

notes: Reference feature Cabeus B crater: 59.6 km diameter, centred 82.26°S 54.58°W.

NASA has not published the location of the peak. Observation point = the highest LOLA elevation (3×3-smoothed) between 0.6 and 1.6 crater radii of the Cabeus B centre, i.e. the most prominent peak adjoining the crater. Provisional reference: it may not coincide with the NASA region.
Near the 80°S edge of LDEM_80S_80M: horizon rays toward the north (away from the pole) leave the DEM after ~40 km instead of 150 km, so distant terrain in those directions is not included.
